description: A local CLI that converts a user's images, text, subtitles, video and audio into one searchable PDF with an invisible OCR/caption layer and an embedded JSON manifest, using optional local tools and trusted runtime plugins. It runs with the user's permissions and has no network listener. Input file contents and names are the untrusted surface; flags, environment and installed plugins are trusted.

attack_classes: path and metadata leaks in shared outputs
downstream_responsibilities: install only trusted plugins; keep plugin search directories trusted; use --no-plugins otherwise
convert untrusted media in an OS sandbox with quotas; set non-zero frame caps
use --profile share before sharing outputs; review content for sensitive data yourself
do not treat manifest SHA-256 values as proof a PDF is unaltered; sign and verify externally
escape text from PDFs, JSON, extract output and stderr before HTML, terminal, shell or database use
put outputs outside the directories you scan
keep FFmpeg, ExifTool, Tesseract, Python and docTR from trusted sources
pre-install docTR weights or use --ocr tesseract/off on offline hosts
do not run two conversions to the same output at once; clean temp dirs after killed runs
treat extract output as unverified for sidecar origin or version-mismatch warnings
treat file base names on the provenance page and in the manifest as attacker-chosen text
plugin authors treat request content as untrusted, write responses atomically and stay in the workspace

known_misuse.pattern: scanning an untrusted tree with defaults, then sharing the PDF
known_misuse.why_unsafe: plugins run, frame caps are off, and the archive profile embeds GPS and camera metadata
known_misuse.instead: --no-plugins, non-zero frame caps, --profile share, inside a sandbox

known_misuse.pattern: using --deny-plugin-kind to block an untrusted plugin
known_misuse.why_unsafe: the plugin's manifest command still runs on every invocation
known_misuse.instead: remove the plugin from the search path or use --no-plugins

known_misuse.pattern: treating the manifest as tamper evidence
known_misuse.why_unsafe: anyone who can edit the PDF can rewrite the manifest to match
known_misuse.instead: sign the PDF and verify the signature

known_misuse.pattern: writing outputs inside the scanned directory
known_misuse.why_unsafe: later scans ingest earlier outputs and their sidecars
known_misuse.instead: write outputs to a separate directory

known_misuse.why_unsafe: OCR text and visible content are not redacted

known_misuse.pattern: running untrusted conversions on a shared host with defaults
known_misuse.why_unsafe: no input size limits and no plugin sandbox
known_misuse.instead: per-job containers with quotas, plus non-zero frame caps

known_non_findings.reported_as: a runtime plugin can read or write any file, open sockets, or use unlimited CPU and memory
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against plugin-host, x-unsandboxed-host-access is the disclaimed os-sandbox property: plugins are trusted native processes with no filesystem, network or resource isolation.
known_non_findings.suppression: actor is an installed anytopdf-plugin-* executable acting through its own process, not its response JSON; no P4 or P5 check bypassed

known_non_findings.reported_as: a plugin whose capability kind is denied still executes
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against plugin-host, x-unexpected-code-execution is the disclaimed capability-filter-as-execution-control property: capability filters control registration, and manifest commands still run during discovery.
known_non_findings.suppression: --no-plugins not set; the only execution is the --anytopdf-manifest command during discovery
